record.original_question: Is the decomposition of the Spin(7) elliptic genus Ell_M(τ, α) into characters of the Shatashvili-Vafa Spin(7) algebra induced by decomposing the topological-twist cohomology H(C∞(M, Ω_ch(M)), Q−_0) into irreducible representations of the SV^Spin7 algebra supplied by the conjectural Spin(7) chiral-de Rham construction?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let M be a compact 8-dimensional Riemannian manifold with holonomy group contained in Spin(7), and let Ω_ch(M) denote the chiral de Rham complex of M, viewed as a sheaf of topological vertex superalgebras on M. The space of global smooth sections C^∞(M, Ω_ch(M)) is conjectured to carry an action of the Shatashvili–Vafa Spin(7) superconformal vertex algebra SV^{Spin(7)} at central charge c = 12, generated (in the N=1 superconformal setting) by additional fields of spin 2 and 5/2 in addition to the N=1 super-Virasoro generators.

Choose one of the topological supercharges Q^-_0 of this SV^{Spin(7)} action and form the cohomology
   H := H(C^∞(M, Ω_ch(M)), Q^-_0),
which inherits an action of SV^{Spin(7)}.

The Spin(7) elliptic genus Ell_M(τ, α) of M admits a decomposition into characters of irreducible representations of SV^{Spin(7)}; the multiplicity functions appearing in this decomposition are mock modular forms canonically attached to M.

Question. Does the character decomposition of Ell_M(τ, α) into irreducible SV^{Spin(7)} characters arise as the graded character of an honest decomposition of H into irreducible representations of SV^{Spin(7)}? Equivalently, do the mock-modular multiplicity functions in the elliptic-genus decomposition equal the graded dimensions of the isotypic components of the SV^{Spin(7)}-module H?
artifact.category_tag: Chiral de Rham complex and Spin(7) elliptic genera
artifact.status_search_result: Web search shows ongoing work on the Shatashvili–Vafa Spin(7) algebra, the Spin(7) chiral de Rham complex, and the character decomposition of the Spin(7) elliptic genus, but no source establishes that the elliptic-genus decomposition is realized by an SV^{Spin(7)}-decomposition of the topological cohomology of the chiral de Rham complex. The underlying construction itself is conjectural in the literature, so the question appears still open.

status_evidence.title: On the Elliptic Genera of Manifolds of Spin(7) Holonomy
status_evidence.snippet: Characters of the Spin(7) extended superconformal algebra are computed and the elliptic genus of a general Spin(7) compactification is decomposed in terms of these characters.
status_evidence.claim: Decomposition of Spin(7) elliptic genus into SV^{Spin(7)} characters is established at the level of characters.

status_evidence.title: Chiral de Rham complex on Riemannian manifolds and special holonomy
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of special-holonomy superconformal structures on global sections of the chiral de Rham complex.
status_evidence.claim: The Spin(7) chiral de Rham construction underlying the question is conjectural and developed in subsequent work.
